Subjects

Islam and modernity

How Muslim thinkers have responded to modern ideas, science and society.

This is the question that most of the archive is about. From the mid-nineteenth century Muslim writers asked how to respond to European power, new sciences, the nation-state and secular ideas: take them in selectively, as Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Muhammad Abduh did, set them aside in the name of a purer Islam, or build a modern of their own, as Iqbal, Malek Bennabi and Fazlur Rahman each argued in different ways.

With close to eight hundred entries, the path below picks one work from each stage of the argument. For the full range, filter the library by era.

Where to begin

A reading order, earliest first. Each title opens the text or the free copy.

  1. 1870 · Book
    A Series of Essays on the Life of Mohammed and Subjects Subsidiary Thereto ↗ Sayyid Ahmad Khan

    Sir Syed answers a hostile English biography of the Prophet, and sets out the modernist case in the process.

  2. 1902 · Book
    Islam and Christianity in Relation to Science and Civilisation ↗ Muḥammad ʿAbduh

    Abduh on whether Islam or Christianity has been the better friend of science and civilisation.

  3. 1934 · Book
    The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam ↗ Muhammad Iqbal

    Iqbal's lectures, the most cited modern statement on rebuilding Muslim thought.

  4. 1949 · Book
    The Conditions of Renaissance ↗ Malek Bennabi

    Bennabi on what a society needs before it can renew itself.

  5. 1978 · Book
    Islam and Secularism ↗ Syed Muhammad Naquib al-Attas

    Al-Attas on secularisation as a problem of knowledge, not only of politics.

  6. 1982 · Book
    Islam and Modernity: Transformation of an Intellectual Tradition ↗ Fazlur Rahman

    Rahman's account of what happened to Muslim intellectual life and how education might repair it.

  7. 2004 · Book
    Western Muslims and the Future of Islam ↗ Tariq Ramadan

    Ramadan's argument for a European Muslim identity built on citizenship and ethics.
